source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two labeled NVAF dose-reduction criteria are present","B":"Reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily whenever any degree of renal impairment is documented clinically","C":"Keep the dose unchanged because age, weight, and serum creatinine never affect NVAF dosing","D":"Increase the dose whenever serum creatinine reaches 1.5 mg/dL because renal clearance is lower"}}
source_row.rationale: For stroke and systemic embolism prevention in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, the current ELIQUIS label recommends 5 mg twice daily for most adults and 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of three criteria are present: age at least 80 years, body weight at most 60 kg, or serum creatinine at least 1.5 mg/dL. The prior item was too broad because apixaban dosing is indication-specific and renal impairment alone is not the universal rule described there.
source_row.source_detail: Current label version 38, section 2.1: NVAF dose 5 mg twice daily; reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of age ≥80 years, body weight ≤60 kg, or serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL are present.
source_row.stem: A client with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation is prescribed apixaban. Which statement about the labeled adult dose-reduction criteria is accurate?
